Coco Lakes, located in the heart of Coconut Creek, is a picturesque community comprising 118 single-family units. This residential enclave offers residents a peaceful and family-friendly living experience. The single-family homes in Coco Lakes are known for their diverse architectural styles, spacious yards, and a sense of community. The neighborhood features well-maintained streets and green spaces, creating a welcoming and aesthetically pleasing atmosphere. With convenient access to top-rated schools, shopping centers, and major highways, Coco Lakes provides a perfect blend of suburban tranquility and urban convenience.

Constructed during the late 1990s, homes in Coco Lakes were built with five star quality construction materials, interesting architectural features, and incredibly flexible floor plans. Many of the homes feature three bedroom or four bedroom floor plans, two car garages, open kitchens, and between 1,500 and 3000 living square feet.

Coconut Creek offers residents a diverse array of amenities and activities. The city boasts well-maintained parks and recreational areas, providing ample opportunities for outdoor activities. The city’s dedication to preserving green spaces and promoting a healthy lifestyle is symbolized by its butterfly gardens and the renowned Butterfly World facility.

Located just west of the Florida Turnpike and south of the Sawgrass Expressway in the heart of Coconut Creek, Coco Lakes is a community comprised of single family homes surrounding an oversized fifty-five acre man-made lake.

blocks.text: College Park is a vibrant neighborhood located just outside of downtown Orlando where you can experience urban living with a small town feel within a larger municipality consisting of 6,119 homes. College Park’s wide selection of services, bungalow-style homes, brick tree-lined streets and many parks and lakes create a vibrant lifestyle and a comfortable place for residents and is a hub for young professionals. College Park offers residents a great mix of older homes and new construction. While Craftsman bungalows and colorful cottages still anchor the neighborhood’s established housing, the community offers a wide variety of styles and sizes from which to choose Smaller single story traditional homes and midcentury ranch style designs are amongst contemporary custom multi-level homes and large Spanish Mediterranean homes that feature decorative architectural flourishes and sleek modern-style homes with imposing facades.

Edgewater Drive, known to locals as simply “The Drive,” offering residents access to an array of popular boutique shops and eclectic eateries. The commercial corridor also hosts popular events throughout the year, from wine strolls to music festivals. Clustered along the main street, Edgewater Drive, are gastropubs, hip boutiques and vintage stores. In addition, the neighborhood is populated with lakes and green spaces.

The affluent College Park neighborhood is known for its 20th-century cottages, abundant green spaces and lakes. Lake Ivanhoe, in particular, is popular for waterskiing, wakeboarding and its views of the downtown skyline. Pocket parks can be found throughout the neighborhood, with Albert Park being the most centrally located. The picturesque urban space features a gazebo and picnic areas in close proximity to the retail and dining along Edgewater Drive. The College Park Neighborhood Center’s amenities include a gymnasium, pool and fitness center. It also offers an afterschool program, summer camp and classes for teens, adults and seniors.

The neighborhood is also home to the Dubsdread, a landmark 18-hole Golf Course, which is a neighborhood landmark that features the oldest public layout in Central Florida. The Tap Room, a community gathering place that serves brunch, lunch and dinner and often features live outdoor music. Located west of I-4, connecting to the theme park attractions, and east of SR-423 and Orange Blossom Trail, College Park is made up of the of some of the finest retailers, award winning restaurants and small businesses. Surrounded by a network of highways and public transportation routes, College Park offers residents easy access to other parts of the city and an ultra-quick commute to downtown. A Sun Rail commuter train station is located just east of the neighborhood at the Advent Health Orlando campus, and there are two others downtown. Orlando’s historic Amtrak station is located just south of downtown, and the city’s international airport is just a 26 minute drive.

blocks.text: 8900 Royal Coblestone Way Boynton Beach, FL 33472

Located in west Boynton Beach, Cobblestone Creek is a family friendly community, on the east side of Lyons Rd. north of Boynton Beach Blvd.,filled with a quiet sense of neighborhood in a luxuriously appointed community. Enter the 24-hour manned gates to find a neighborhood filled with shimmering blue waterways, cascading waterfalls, mature palm trees, and colorful tropical plantings. These one and two story homes are comprised of three to six bedroom floor plans and range in size from 2,700 square feet to just under 4,500 square feet and most homes have serene views of one of the three large lakes and fountains.

All residents of Cobblestone Creek have access to fantastic neighborhood features such as a well appointed clubhouse, large swimming pool with an outdoor spa overlooking a beautiful lake, a state-of-the-art fitness center and a clubroom. Cobblestone Creek also offers 24-hour security and onsite management for your safety and convenience. Homeowner association fees in Cobblestone Creek remain low and include 24-hour security, basic cable, and maintenance of all common areas. Cobblestone Creek residents enjoy year-round use of their private swimming pools, spillover spas, oversized lanais, and summer kitchens.

Canyon Town Center is only one mile away, so within a short walk you have a Publix Super Market, banks, salons, a pharmacy and several restaurants. The Boynton Beach Mall and Town Center is only eight miles away,

Loxahatchee National Wildlife Refuge is just a 10-minute drive away, with over 221 square miles of Everglades habitat it is home to the American Alligator and the endangered Everglade snail kite. Florida’s Turnpike is just a few minutes’ drive from Cobblestone Creek, head North for 15 miles and spend a day in the tropical city of Lake Worth or head South for just 14 miles to Boca Raton.

A 600-seat theater showcases ballet, opera and lectures as well as in-house productions. Coral Lakes also features an on-site cafe serving breakfast and lunch. Dine indoors in climate-controlled comfort, or al fresca on the terrace that overlooks a lake and the pool.

Coral Lakes is accessible to area amenities The Boynton Beach Mall and Town Center is under seven miles away with many great restaurants. Boynton Beach Harbor or Oceanfront Park Beach and Links at Boynton Beach Golf are 20 minutes away. Situated in Boynton Beach on Imperial Isle Drive, Coral Lakes is within a quick commute to historic downtown Delray, West Palm Beach City Place and Boca Raton's Mizner Park, which are all desirable destinations for shopping, dining and entertainment. All are outfitted with modern fixtures, a variety of parking options and beautifully manicured gardens. There are15 lakes scattered throughout the neighborhood alongside walking trails, ensuring serene views for most the homes, on 580 acres.

Coral Cove and Regal Shores have condominiums. Coral Cove has four-story buildings and Regal Shores is comprised of two and four-story buildings. Both have reserved outdoor parking spaces and offer 1,509 to 1,869 square feet of living space with two bedrooms and two bathrooms.

Egret Point and Royal Landings feature attached patio homes, which contain two homes under one roof and have attached one-car garages with one to three bedrooms, and offer 1,600 to 1,780 square feet. Crystal Pointe features coach homes and villa homes, also with garages and offer 1,569 to 1,861 square feet. The coach homes have one residence over another in each home, and the villas are homes connected side by side.

Regency Cove and Tuscany are two neighborhoods that have free-standing single-family homes, which are the largest residences in Coral Lakes. Both include attached two-car garages and offer 1,600 to 2,500 square feet of living space. These homes are single-story with two or three bedrooms and two or three bathrooms.

Coral Lakes residents have access to the amazing 72,000 square feet clubhouse that sits in the center of Coral Lakes. Activities are arranged daily throughout the year, including shows, movies, and a large array of social groups and classes. Billiards and tennis competitions, paddle ball courts, and  shuffleboard courts are also available with a full-time activities director. There are 5 outdoor satellite pools and an indoor glass enclosed pool, a fully equipped fitness center and aerobics studio, whirlpool, sauna, steam room, meeting room, 7 card rooms and a lounge that functions as a library with computer stations. A 600-seat theater showcases ballet, opera and lectures as well as in-house productions. Coral Lakes also features an on-site cafe serving breakfast and lunch. Dine indoors in climate-controlled comfort, or al fresca on the terrace that overlooks a lake and the pool.

Coral Lakes is accessible to area amenities The Boynton Beach Mall and Town Center is under seven miles away with many great restaurants. Boynton Beach Harbor or Oceanfront Park Beach and Links at Boynton Beach Golf are 20 minutes away. Situated in Boynton Beach on Imperial Isle Drive, Coral Lakes is within a quick commute to historic downtown Delray, West Palm Beach City Place and Boca Raton's Mizner Park, which are all desirable destinations for shopping, dining and entertainment. The area has plenty of nature and wildlife nearby.

/neighborhood/coquina-key.description: Coquina Key Homes for Sale Pinellas County Homes for.

blocks.text: Coquina Key Dr St. Petersburg, FL 33705

Coquina Key homes are conveniently located in the Southeast area of Pinellas County near Beach Drive. Surrounded by Big Bayou to the northwest, Little Bayou to the southwest, and Tampa Bay to the east, Coquina Key, known as "The Friendly Island" offers all of the Florida's most stunning views from the herons and turtles in the marshy creeks to the dolphins and pelicans of the open water.

It is located just 4 miles south of Downtown St Petersburg waterfront and the interstate I-275. Coquina Key is populated by a mixture of single-family homes, with townhomes and condos at Waterside, with fantastic views of the Big Bayou and great amenities including a heated pool, hot tub, fitness center and bar. Single-family homes make up a little less than half of the properties with up to 2 car garages. Homes range in size from 2 bedroom, 2 bath layouts with 900 to1,500 square feet of living area to 4 bedroom homes with 3,317 square feet of living area. A typical Coquina Key home is a 3 bedroom, 2 bath layout with 1,500 feet of living space. About one-quarter of the homes are waterfront properties located on quite creeks or on the wide open water. Most of the homes were built in the 1950s and 1060s with homes built in 2016.

The single family homes for sale in Coquina Key are located close to some of the best shopping and restaurants in the area, close to St. Pete Beach and Tierra Verde, and within walking distance to several schools. Downtown St. Petersburg is only about 4 miles north and a minute ride traffic permitting. Downtown is the mecca of culture and dining in the Pinellas County area. Enjoy easy access to a wide variety of museums, theater groups, and great local dining areas located downtown.

Boat lovers will love living on Coquina Key. Walk out to your lift, drop in your boat and you're out to the Bay in minutes. The Gulf of Mexico is just around Pinellas Point. St. Pete Beach is just 8 miles west of Coquina Key. Just south of St. Pete Beach is Pass-A-Grille Beach, a big favorite with locals and a really special place. It is very laid-back with a lot less tourism than Clearwater Beach or St. Pete Beach.
Coquina Key Park with lots of green spaces is located at the northern tip of the island at 3595 Locust St SE, St. Petersburg, FL 33705. It is a family park and is dog friendly.

blocks.text: Coral Key Harbor is a prestigious waterfront subdivision located in the charming city of Lighthouse Point. An exclusive community offering a unique blend of luxury living and a boater's paradise, Coral Key Harbor boasts a prime location with direct access to the sparkling waters to the Intracoastal Waterway. The neighborhood is situated on a series of canals characterized by its picturesque waterfront homes, many of which feature private docks and stunning views of the water. Known for its stunning waterways, impressive homes, and convenient location, Coral Key Harbor is an ideal destination for those seeking a luxurious and comfortable lifestyle.

Coral Key is an expansive community of 502 single family homes with a wide selection of floor plans with homes that offer two to six bedrooms and open floor plans, updated bathrooms, large master suites, and more. Some of the estate homes are located along the water’s edge with have boat dockage. The community is north of NE 45 Street, east of US1 and west of the Hillsboro Mile.

Coral Key Villas is a luxury, waterfront community located in the city of Lighthouse Point, featuring Mediterranean-style homes with more than 6,000 square feet of living space. Many homes in Coral Key Villas boast private tropical pools and deep-water docks.

Residents can enjoy the best of both worlds, living in a tranquil waterfront retreat while enjoying easy access to the vibrant city life of nearby Fort Lauderdale. Lighthouse Point is a great community for those who enjoy boating, fishing and water sports. The community also features a range of parks and green spaces, as well as convenient access to shopping centers, restaurants, beaches and entertainment venues. Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport is close by.

/neighborhood/coral-ridge-isles.description: Search Homes For Sale in Coral Ridge Isles in Fort Lauderdale.

blocks.text: Coral Ridge Isles consists of nearly 1,000 homes bounded by Commercial Boulevard to the South, Cypress Creek Road to the North, Dixie Highway to the West and NE 18th Avenue to the East. Many of the 769 homes are located on waterfront canals with ocean access for boats that can get under lower fixed bridges. There are a variety of residential options, including single-family homes, condominiums, and townhomes. Homes range from 500 square feet to over 3,500 square feet in living area.This charming neighborhood boasts well-maintained properties set against lush landscaping, creating a serene and visually appealing environment. With its friendly and tropical streets, Coral Ridge sits in Fort Lauderdale’s north side with finger canals on waterfront properties on the neighborhood’s western edge. The beach is just a couple of minutes East on Commercial Boulevard.

The community is in close proximity to schools, hospitals, restaurants and shopping. Lined with mature Royal Palms the streets are clean and quiet. Sitting along two coastal cities, Coral Ridge Isles straddles the line between two coastal cities, reaping the benefits of its central location to beaches, restaurants, entertainment and excellent schools. The neighborhood is backed by its close proximity to Pompano Beach and Cypress Creek Canal which features a convenient alternative to the more crowded shopping and entertainment districts.

Most homes in Coral Ridge Isles are single-story ranches. The majority of houses in the neighborhood have seen renovations and remodels since the initial buildout, bringing color and flair to the community with Spanish eclectic designs. Many homes in Coral Ridge Isles boast waterfront views, with in-ground pools and lush landscaping.

Floranada Park features a baseball field, basketball and volleyball courts. There are many restaurants to choose from within a 5 mile radius. Residents are within close proximity to both I-95 and US-1 where they can easily entertain the benefits of Pompano Beach and Cypress Creek Canal and they are just a 20 minute drive from downtown Fort Lauderdale. Fort Lauderdale is also well served by Broward County Transit covering more than 400 square miles of routes that will serve Coral Ridge Isles residents well. The downtown area, centered around Las Olas Boulevard, features a mix of modern skyscrapers and historic architecture, offering upscale shopping, dining, and entertainment options. Fort Lauderdale’s diverse cultural scene, featuring museums, theaters, and art galleries, contributes to the city’s overall vibrancy.

blocks.text: Cormorant Point is an active adult subdivision is located within the master-planned Golf Hammock community. Residents enjoy low-maintenance homes in a beautifully landscaped setting, and some homes enjoy scenic views of the 18-hole championship golf course. Residents living in Cormorant Point have the option to purchase a membership to enjoy the pool and golf amenities at the Golf Hammock clubhouse.

Homes in the community include attached villas that range in size from approximately 1,390 square feet to 2,297 square feet in living area with two bedrooms, two bathrooms, and an attached one-and-a-half or two-car garage and single-family homes. These homes offer 1,193 square feet to 2,779 square feet of living area with two bedrooms, two or two-and-a-half bathrooms, and an attached two-car garage.

Although Cormorant Point doesn't have its own amenities, 55+ residents can purchase an optional membership to use the pool and golf amenities in Golf Hammock. The clubhouse of Golf Hammock provides plenty of social spaces where neighbors can get together for fun activities and events. Homeowners can socialize in the multi-purpose room, grab a bite to eat in the restaurant, or buy the latest gear in the pro shop. Residents will also love the indoor golf practice facilities that are perfect for honing their skills before heading out to the course. Outside amenities include a pool, tennis courts and walking and biking trails.

Everyday conveniences are close by with major roads like Highway 98 for easy commute. There are plenty of recreational opportunities and attractions close by as well like Lake Jackson, Lake Sebring, Highlands Hammock State Park, several golf courses, Sebring International Raceway, and horse riding stables. Avon Park that can be reached in 20 minutes, Winter Haven is an hour's drive, or Lakeland is about an hour-and-a-half away. For long distance travel, residents can fly out of Sebring Regional Airport or Sarasota-Bradenton International Airport.

blocks.text: The Corinthians Jupiter is an expansive, six-story, oceanfront condominium built in 1985. The units are staggered out in a V shape so each condo has an ocean view. The condominium encompasses almost 500 feet of oceanfront, directly across from the Jupiter beach.

The Corinthians, Jupiter oceanfront condos, allow you to participate in the Jupiter lifestyle without the upkeep associated with a single-family home, and there are very few single-family homes as close to the ocean as The Corinthians. The 58 units in The Corinthians offer two-bedroom, two bath units with 1,460-1656 square feet of living space and three bedroom, two and a half bath units with 1,893 square feet, and penthouse units of 2732 square feet some with direct oceanfront views. Sitting behind the Corinthians is Olympus, a Jupiter beachside community of single family homes. The condos facing south are the preferred units as they overlook single family homes and the higher floors look way down towards Juno Beach. The construction is CBS, and the community features an underground parking with deeded spaces. Some units have two spaces, some have one.

Amenities include pool, sauna, tennis court, billiard room, men's and women's saunas and fully equipped exercise room with TV and VCR. Heated pool with hot and cold outside showers and unground parking.

While the main attraction is the proximity to the beach, all condos in Jupiter were built across Beach Road from the beach, but most condos in The Corinthians have fabulous views of the clear and warm Atlantic Ocean where the section of the beach is considered “dog-friendly” and the Friends of Jupiter Beach encourage owners to bring their canine companions to enjoy the beach, too.

The Corinthians is located close to entertainment and medical facilities. It is10 minutes to the north to reach the Town of Jupiter and 10 minutes to the south to reach Palm Beach Gardens. Centrally located between US 1 and A1A and close to Maltz Theatre, Jupiter Beach Resort, Jupiter Inlet, Jupiter Lighthouse, shopping and restaurants.

blocks.text: Cory Lake Isles in Tampa Bay is a premier community boasting elegantly brick paved roads, lush tropical foliage, and over 919 beautiful executive homes tucked into the city's far northeast corner with access to lakes and lots of conservation areas. Cory Lake Isles is set along hand-laid brick streets, landscaped isles, and wide boulevards lined with Canary Palms and decorative lamp post lighting. Bordered by 17,000 acres of protected woodlands, residents have views of Cory Lake and surrounding conservation areas. The streets of the gated community feature palm trees and well-manicured lawns and the low-traffic streets. Shopping, dining options and medical facilities are nearby.

Home design is heavily influenced by the Spanish Mediterranean flair with ornate facades, terra cotta roofs and brick driveways common. The community's aesthetics are protected and maintained as homes are painted to adhere to the approved color palette: neutrals, greens, ivory, yellows and greys. As the majority of homes are on the water, private piers and boats are common in backyards. Homes range from 3-6 bedrooms and from 1,710 to 7,168 square feet with the average single family home in Cory Lake is 3,472 square feet in living area.

Cory Lake, a 165-acre skiable lake crowned with 10 miles of shoreline, is a recreational epicenter. The lake and its surrounding canals create a haven for outdoor activities, from jet-skiing and canoeing to sailing and fishing. An annual boat parade and fishing tournaments are held on the lake, as well as other special events including holiday and themed parties at the Beach Club, a community center on its shores.

Residents have access to a picturesque community pool, which features lap lanes and a waterslide. There are tennis, pickleball, basketball courts and even hockey. A small beach area is located behind the community center. It is a great place for residents who love boating and all kinds of water activities in an exclusive community. Parks in the area include Landing Village Playground with basketball, tennis and picnic area, Trace Village Playground, with playground, basketball and picnic area and Estuary Playground.

Cory Lake Isles maintains an enviable location with easy access to major travel routes like I-75, I-4, and I-275. This convenient location means the neighborhood is just minutes from the offerings of downtown Tampa, the USF campus, Moffitt Center, and a host of state-of-the-art business parks. Tampa International Airport is 48 minuets away.

Cory Lake Isles in Tampa Bay is a premier community boasting elegantly brick paved roads, lush tropical foliage, and over 919 beautiful executive homes tucked into the city's far northeast corner with access to lakes and lots of conservation areas. Cory Lake Isles is set along  hand-laid brick streets, landscaped isles, and wide boulevards lined with Canary Palms and decorative lamp post lighting. Bordered by 17,000 acres of protected woodlands, residents have views of Cory Lake and surrounding conservation areas. The streets of the gated community feature palm trees and well-manicured lawns and the low-traffic streets. Shopping, dining options and medical facilities are nearby. 

Home design is heavily influenced by the Spanish Mediterranean flair with ornate facades, terra cotta roofs and brick driveways common. The community's aesthetics are protected and maintained as homes are painted to adhere to the approved color palette: neutrals, greens, ivory, yellows and greys. As the majority of homes are on the water, private piers and boats are common in backyards. Homes range from 3-6 bedrooms and from 1,710 to 7,168 square feet with the average single family home in Cory Lake is 3,472 square feet in living area.

Cory Lake, a 165-acre skiable lake crowned with 10 miles of shoreline, is a recreational epicenter. The lake and its surrounding canals create a haven for outdoor activities, from jet-skiing and canoeing to sailing and fishing. An annual boat parade and fishing tournaments are held on the lake, as well as other special events including holiday and themed parties at the Beach Club, a community center on its shores. 

Residents have access to a picturesque community pool, which features lap lanes and a waterslide. There are tennis, pickleball, basketball courts and even hockey. A small beach area is located behind the community center.  It is a great place for residents who love boating and all kinds of water activities in an exclusive community. Parks in the area include Landing Village Playground with basketball, tennis and picnic area, Trace Village Playground, with playground, basketball and picnic area and Estuary Playground.

 Cory Lake Isles maintains an enviable location with easy access to major travel routes like I-75, I-4, and I-275. This convenient location means the neighborhood is just minutes from the offerings of downtown Tampa, the USF campus, Moffitt Center, and a host of state-of-the-art business parks. Tampa International Airport is 48 minuets away.

blocks.text: The Country Club of Ocala attracts friendly, family-oriented people from all walks of life and age groups. This creates a warm and welcoming environment that has proven to foster friendships as well as business relationships. Homes are priced from $250,000 to $1,000,000. Residents can play golf on the 18-hole championship Golf Course or lounge by our pool with friends. With first-class golf, tennis, fitness, and dining, there is never a shortage of events and activities for all ages and interests. Gold amenities include practice range, golf shop and instruction. For health and wellness, there are personal trainers, group fitness, weight, cardio, physical therapy, massage, water aerobics, yoga and Pilates. Social activities include cards, crafts, theatre, dancing and wine tasting.

Golf Club restaurant offers lunch Wednesday through Saturday, and dinner Thursday through Saturday. Meals are served in one of the two dining rooms overlooking the Club's trademark waterfall and stream, unless you prefer the scenic vista views from our canyon-style wrap-around porch. The Country Club of Ocala is available for meetings or special events.

Types of memberships from golf, aquatics, and tennis, to fitness or simply to socialize offer all members the complete Country Club experience. A Full Family Membership entitles the Member, spouse, and all unmarried children under twenty-three years of age, who are living at home or in college, to the following Club privileges: full Clubhouse, Tennis, Pool, fitness facility, and unlimited golf with no payment of green fees. A Junior Family Membership is available to those individuals aged forty-nine and under, entitling the Member, spouse and all unmarried children under twenty-three years of age, who are living at home or in college, to the same privileges as a full family member. There are Corporate and Corporate Associate memberships as well as Tennis and Social memberships.
The Country Club of Ocala is conveniently located to shopping, dining and medical facilities.

blocks.text: Cresswind Lakewood Ranch is a gated, active adult, master planned community in Lakewood Ranch in Manatee County Florida. Cresswind features 649 new homes designed for active adults on 250 acres, with homes ranging from 1524 square feet to 3574 square feet in living space. One of only two age-restricted communities in Lakewood Ranch, Cresswind sets itself apart with its award-winning lifestyle programs are based upon the cornerstones of fitness, relationships, education and entertainment. The Island Collection offers eight home models that range from 1,827 to 3,067 square feet. The Coastal Collection features eight floor plans that range from 2,384 to 3,574 square feet.

There is pickleball, tennis, bocce court as well as walking trails and community parks and dog park.

Living in Cresswind Lakewood Ranch also means residents get access to all of the other amenities and activities offered within the Lakewood Ranch master-planned community. blocks.text: 6231 Palm Vista St Port Orange, FL 32128

The gated community forms the desirable selection of homes in Cypress Head being positioned on more than 670 acres of breathtaking tropical landscaping. The neighborhood is comprised of master-planned townhomes backing onto wondrous natural preserves as well as custom estate homes featuring an interesting blend of original construction and newly designed Mediterranean and Tuscan-style properties with unbelievable views of the lakefront. With rows of mature trees casting a majestic shadow over the community’s numerous water features, life in Cypress Head offers waking up to your own personal piece of serenity. Homes feature 2-5 bedrooms and range from 1,618-3,167 square feet of living area. The larger single-family homes are situated in two subdivisions: The Keys and The Lakes, and range in size from 2,000-square feet to over 5,000-square feet.

Cypress Head is conveniently located on Holmberg Road, between Riverside and Parkside Drives. There is shopping and activity at The Pavilion, a few miles north, including department stores like Target and restaurants like Malibu Beach Bar. People in Cypress Head don't have to go far for relaxation or activity, but they have a convenient 10-mile drive to the oceanfront.

Amenities at the Community Clubhouse include tennis, pickleball and swimming pool. Inside the clubhouse with community events and club meetings. Airport Road Park, where they shoot hoops and play on the covered playground also has multiple tennis and pickleball courts. Hikers and mountain bikers head across Interstate 95 to Doris Leeper Spruce Creek Trailhead for miles of sandy trails through dense mangrove forests.

The area is also revered as a thriving golf community with Cypress Head Golf Club being an attractive green owned by the city of Port Orange. Amenities at the club include a driving range, putting green, pitching and chipping area, golf school academy, teaching pro, restaurant, and banquet facilities. The clubhouse and community pool are popular destinations for golfers and their families. The museums and shops downtown is the perfect way to enjoy the hidden treasures found throughout the area and the world-renowned Daytona International Speedway isn’t far either. Situated along the banks of the Halifax River, Volusia County is one of the most leisurely diverse areas in Florida.

A host of entertainment and dining options are also available along nearby Taylor Road, which is home to various retail stores and boutique shops, restaurants, and bars. Residents can also visit nearby attractions, including the Marine Science Center, New Smyrna Museum of History, and Gamble Place Historic District. Cypress Head locals can also find plenty of parks to visit outside of the community, including Spruce Creek Park, Bushman Park, and Airport Road Park. Daytona Beach is just 25-minutes away and Orlando is only an hour drive.

blocks.text: Living in Davis Islands, Tampa, FL offers a unique and vibrant lifestyle. Nestled in the sparkling waters of Hillsborough Bay, this exclusive island community provides a perfect blend of natural beauty and modern conveniences. Across the Columbia Drive Bridge from Tampa, in Hillsborough Bay, sits Davis Islands, a pair of islands making up one neighborhood. With its picturesque waterfront views, lush green spaces, and charming tree-lined streets, Davis Islands offers a peaceful and serene environment for residents to enjoy. The neighborhood is made up of large Mediterranean single family homes, newer contemporary homes as well as townhomes. Most homes are on roads with only residential traffic and feature lawns and private driveways. Many of the properties are listed under the National Register of Historic Places, which adds to the incredible desirability of this area. Mature trees shade the spacious and paved sidewalks.

The island is home to a close-knit community that takes pride in its well-maintained parks, inviting beaches, and excellent recreational amenities. Davis Islands truly offers a delightful balance of tranquility and urban connectivity. Residents enjoy Davis Island Beach, Davis Island Park and walk alongside Davis Island Village.

The island is conveniently located just 2 miles from downtown Tampa, providing easy access to the city's vibrant cultural scene, shopping districts, and employment opportunities. The historic Davis Islands are known for their views of downtown Tampa, as well as lavish, pastel-colored Mediterranean-style buildings dating from the 1920s. Relaxing spots include Dog Beach, a canine-friendly stretch of sand with views of boats and yachts, and Davis Islands Park, a green space with kids’ play equipment. An eclectic mix of cafes and pubs is clustered along East Davis Boulevard. The Davis Island Yacht Club is a private, member-owned yacht club situated at the south end of Davis Islands.

Davis Islands is a mix of beautiful residential and retail areas all encompassed by parks, green-space and stunning water views. Davis Islands is the home to Peter O. Knight Airport, Davis Islands Yacht Club, Tampa General Hospital, Sandra Freedman Tennis Complex and the Roy Jenkins aquatic center. Also on the Islands are the Marjorie Park and Marjorie Park Municipal Yacht Basin. Marjorie Park was donated to the City of Tampa and named by Davis after his wife Marjorie Merritt Davis.

blocks.text: Dixieland is one of Lakeland’s most colorful and vibrant neighborhoods, with many bungalow homes originally built between the 1920s and 1940s, amongst generous green spaces, churches, schools, and a growing retail corridor of vintage shops, restaurants, art galleries and coffeehouses. Lake Hunter offers an eclectic mix of shopping and dining options. Vintage shops are a growing industry in the Dixieland district, selling everything from knick-knacks to clothing and furniture. It is one of the city’s most traditional neighborhoods, with a grid pattern of streets and alleys, a mature tree canopy, and historic lights, all of which add to the historic atmosphere. Lakeland’s art scene is booming, with the local neighborhood association sponsoring Dixieland’s Alley Fest, a daylong event featuring small businesses and local artists setting up shop in Lakeland’s alleys. Lake Hunter also offers many performance venues. Dixieland historic district is described as an exciting, diverse, and up-and-coming place to call home.

Of the many amenities, Union Hall hosts community events, including concerts, while Pink Piano is a more specialized event space for live music. Both the Polk Museum of Art and Frank Lloyd Wright Visitor Center are about a mile northeast off Lake Morton. The nearby lakes offer a wider range of outdoor recreation for the residents. Lake Hollingsworth is just south of the neighborhood, and Thomas B. Mack Park is next to it with scenic boardwalks and wildlife. The Lakeland Country Club features a lakefront Veranda Bar, along with amenities like a resort-style pool, fitness center and tennis courts. Closer to home, Dobbins Park’s playground, pavilion and field are popular for parties and after-school playtime with Drane Park offering a more low key atmosphere with relaxed green space and shaded with Spanish moss.

The community has evolved through the years and today boasts approximately 750 residential homes, condominium units, golf villas, and single-family detached homes. /sellers-ready.description: Our staging tips are just the beginning of the expert advice and knowledge we can use to help you successfully sell your home. Call us at.

blocks.text: 10 Tips to Stage Your Home and WOW Your Buyers

Getting ready to sell your home in Treasure Coast? Before you start showing your home to buyers, take time to give your home some love - even the simplest home staging and sprucing can be the difference between a buyer that walks away and a buyer that's impressed. These DIY staging tips can really make your home stand out from the crowd.

The outside of your home is just as important as the inside. Spend some time giving your home's exterior some love to create a sense of welcoming - so that your buyers are impressed before they even leave the car!

Before a buyer will set foot inside, they have to be impressed by the exterior of your home. So spend some time making your home welcoming and attractive. Powerwash your siding and driveway, mow the lawn, weed or prune the garden, or plant some bright flowers. Wash your windows, replace old house numbers, or replace a tired mailbox.

An extension of your curb appeal is your porch. Tidy up any furniture, buy a new welcome mat, add some potted flowers, and replace your doorknob. Add a tasteful wreath to your door and leave your porch light on in the evenings, especially if you will be showing at night.

Whether you have a large backyard or a cozy balcony, your outdoor areas should not only be attractive, they should be inviting. Help your buyers to envision a lifestyle by adding seating or dining areas such as chair and tables, a hammock, or even a fire pit. Make sure gardens are cleaned up, the lawn is mown, and any fallen leaves or branches are tidied up.
Nothing turns off a buyer like persistent maintenance problems, lingering repair projects, or a home that's just not clean! Don't lose out on a sale for an easily preventable reason!

Nothing is more intimidating to a buyer than walking into an incomplete project! No missing floorboards, crooked shingles, cracked windows, or any other sign that anything needs to be replaced or repaired. Your home should appear in good maintenance from top to bottom.

Take some time to go through your closets, shelves, cabinets, and counters to clear out anything that's taking up space or making your rooms appear cramped, crowded, or dirty. Donate clothes, partially empty your closets and cabinets to make them appear larger, even rent a storage unit for furniture that is too large, unsightly, or mismatched.

It might not be the most fun part, but it is an absolute necessity that your home sparkle. Get all those hard-to-reach places, scrub dingy tiles and grout, deep clean the showers and tubs. If you're not a fan of cleaning, hire a professional to help. The results will be worth the expense. If you have a pet, you may want to steam clean your rugs or add some type of fragrance, such as soft-scented candles or potpourri, to mask pet odors.
Now that you've created curb appeal and tackled the basics, it's time to start looking for ways to impress your buyers and make your home stand apart from the crowd.

Your home might have a certain style that you find tasteful - but not all home buyers have the same tastes in decor. Neutral and simple are always best. Repaint any bold or bright colored walls with neutral colors. Remove any personal decor and replace with tasteful yet neutral art and centerpieces. You want to create the sense of a home that's lived in but not yours, as the idea is to allow buyers to imagine their own personalizations in your home.

Placement of furniture can change the whole feel of a room. Your furniture should not overcrowd the room or leave it feeling too open. Floating the furniture away from the walls can actually make rooms feel larger and create a cozy, conversational feel.
Now's the fun part - the detailed staging and decorating that adds that "wow" factor, that sparkle, that little bit of something special. Just be sure to keep it simple!

Make your home warm and welcoming by increasing the lighting - both natural and artificial - throughout your home. Open windows if the weather is nice, or at least pull back the drapes to let in as much natural light as possible. Increase the wattage of the bulbs in your lamps and fixtures, and aim for three types of lighting in every room - ambient (overhead), task (reading or under-cabinet lights), and accent (table or floor lamps).

Your decor might be neutral, but that doesn't mean it has to be boring. Bring in bright splashes of color in the form of potted plants, clipped flowers, or fall branches. This can help increase the sense of warmth and welcoming throughout the home.

If you're ready to sell your Treasure Coast home, then it's time to contact Real Estate of Florida. These staging tips are just the beginning of the expert advice and knowledge we can use to help you successfully sell your home. Contact us today and let's list your home.

10 Tips to Stage Your Home and WOW Your Buyers

Getting ready to sell your home in Treasure Coast? Before you start showing your home to buyers, take time to give your home some love - even the simplest home staging and sprucing can be the difference between a buyer that walks away and a buyer that's impressed. These DIY staging tips can really make your home stand out from the crowd.

The Exterior

The outside of your home is just as important as the inside. Spend some time giving your home's exterior some love to create a sense of welcoming - so that your buyers are impressed before they even leave the car!

Create curb appeal:

Before a buyer will set foot inside, they have to be impressed by the exterior of your home. So spend some time making your home welcoming and attractive. Powerwash your siding and driveway, mow the lawn, weed or prune the garden, or plant some bright flowers. Wash your windows, replace old house numbers, or replace a tired mailbox.

Make your porch welcoming:

An extension of your curb appeal is your porch. Tidy up any furniture, buy a new welcome mat, add some potted flowers, and replace your doorknob. Add a tasteful wreath to your door and leave your porch light on in the evenings, especially if you will be showing at night.

Spruce up outdoor areas:

Whether you have a large backyard or a cozy balcony, your outdoor areas should not only be attractive, they should be inviting. Help your buyers to envision a lifestyle by adding seating or dining areas such as chair and tables, a hammock, or even a fire pit. Make sure gardens are cleaned up, the lawn is mown, and any fallen leaves or branches are tidied up.

Cleaning and Repairs

Nothing turns off a buyer like persistent maintenance problems, lingering repair projects, or a home that's just not clean! Don't lose out on a sale for an easily preventable reason!

Finish repair projects:

Nothing is more intimidating to a buyer than walking into an incomplete project! No missing floorboards, crooked shingles, cracked windows, or any other sign that anything needs to be replaced or repaired. Your home should appear in good maintenance from top to bottom.

Clear out the clutter:

Take some time to go through your closets, shelves, cabinets, and counters to clear out anything that's taking up space or making your rooms appear cramped, crowded, or dirty. Donate clothes, partially empty your closets and cabinets to make them appear larger, even rent a storage unit for furniture that is too large, unsightly, or mismatched.

Deep clean EVERYTHING:

It might not be the most fun part, but it is an absolute necessity that your home sparkle. Get all those hard-to-reach places, scrub dingy tiles and grout, deep clean the showers and tubs. If you're not a fan of cleaning, hire a professional to help. The results will be worth the expense. If you have a pet, you may want to steam clean your rugs or add some type of fragrance, such as soft-scented candles or potpourri, to mask pet odors.

Interior Decor

Now that you've created curb appeal and tackled the basics, it's time to start looking for ways to impress your buyers and make your home stand apart from the crowd.

Depersonalize your decor:

Your home might have a certain style that you find tasteful - but not all home buyers have the same tastes in decor. Neutral and simple are always best. Repaint any bold or bright colored walls with neutral colors. Remove any personal decor and replace with tasteful yet neutral art and centerpieces. You want to create the sense of a home that's lived in but not yours, as the idea is to allow buyers to imagine their own personalizations in your home.

Create balance with furniture:

Placement of furniture can change the whole feel of a room. Your furniture should not overcrowd the room or leave it feeling too open. Floating the furniture away from the walls can actually make rooms feel larger and create a cozy, conversational feel.

The Final Details

Now's the fun part - the detailed staging and decorating that adds that "wow" factor, that sparkle, that little bit of something special. Just be sure to keep it simple!

Increase your lighting:

Make your home warm and welcoming by increasing the lighting - both natural and artificial - throughout your home. Open windows if the weather is nice, or at least pull back the drapes to let in as much natural light as possible. Increase the wattage of the bulbs in your lamps and fixtures, and aim for three types of lighting in every room - ambient (overhead), task (reading or under-cabinet lights), and accent (table or floor lamps).

Bring the outdoors inside:

Your decor might be neutral, but that doesn't mean it has to be boring. Bring in bright splashes of color in the form of potted plants, clipped flowers, or fall branches. This can help increase the sense of warmth and welcoming throughout the home.

If you're ready to sell your Treasure Coast home, then it's time to contact Real Estate of Florida. These staging tips are just the beginning of the expert advice and knowledge we can use to help you successfully sell your home. Contact us today and let's list your home.

blocks.text: Steps to Selling a Home in Treasure Coast

Thinking of selling your home in Treasure Coast? It's important to understand that if you expect to make money on your home, you've got to give yourself plenty of time to prepare, and that can mean starting to plan months ahead of the date you'd actually like to move out of your home. Here's what to expect when you list your home in Treasure Coast.
Step 1: Find an Experienced Treasure Coast Agent

This is a crucial first step! Enlisting the help of an experienced agent who understands your needs to guide you through the process will save you time and a lot of headache - and will of course get your home sold more quickly and for more money than trying to list your home on your own.
Find out more about our qualifications and experience!

Your real estate agent will do a thorough walkthrough of your home and will likely make recommendations on both minor and major repairs or improvements you should consider. Additionally, be proactive about any known maintenance issues to your home, as these will surface during an inspection.

Value-boosting home improvements can include projects such as painting your home (inside or outside), refinishing hardwood floors, fixing or replacing your roof or siding, installing a new garage door or front door, doing some gardening or landscaping, updating or repairing your HVAC system, or even performing minor kitchen and bathroom repairs, such as updating flooring, resurfacing cabinets, installing new hardware and fixtures, and replacing or resurfacing countertops.

Another crucial step to ensuring the highest return on your valuable investment in the shortest amount of time is finding a competitive price. You will want to consider the price of nearby homes that have recently sold, the prices of nearby homes currently on the market, and the condition and location of your specific home. Request a neighborhood sold report and work with your agent to find the right listing price.

Hopefully, you have already started decluttering some of the bigger collections of unused furniture and other items stored in your attic, basement, or closets. Continue to work through your home, removing clutter, junk, and even personal decor. Start deep cleaning your home, really targeting the forgotten nooks and crannies.
Then, work with your agent to stage your home so that it is neat, welcoming, and depersonalized (allowing your buyers to picture their own personal touches in their potential new home).
Lastly, take professional photographs that will highlight your home's best features and give buyers a great impression of your home - right from their computer, tablet, or phone.

The key to selling a home is in finding the right buyers, and that requires a lot of marketing and advertising. This is where working with a skilled agent can really pay off. Skilled listing agents are skilled marketers. They know where to find the best buyers for your home, and they have access to a wealth of resources, including online listing services, print advertising distribution, large social media followings, even local agent networks.

In addition to scheduled open houses, your home can be shown at any time, so be prepared. Keep it neat, clean, organized, and staged. Don't leave dirty dishes or laundry lying around, be sure to dust and vacuum regularly, and promptly address any potential clutter buildups. Additionally, you should be ready to clear out of the house during showings to avoid making buyers uncomfortable.
Step 7: Negotiate and Accept an Offer

If a buyer wants to buy your home, they will make you a written offer, which usually states how much they'll pay, their mortgage amount, closing and occupancy dates, and any contingencies. You can either accept the offer or negotiate for different terms.

Negotiations can include your own contingencies, such as a first right of refusal if your buyer's offer is contingent on selling their home, making the offer contingent on you buying another home, or adding contingencies for closing and occupancy dates or buyer financing.
Step 8: Sign a Purchase and Sale Agreement

Once you and the buyer have agreed upon an offer, you will both sign a legal contract called a Purchase and Sale Agreement. This outlines the specific terms, conditions, and contingencies of the home sale.

Next, the buyer will hire an inspector to ensure that no major repairs will be needed after they buy the house. The inspector will go through every inch of the house, paying particular attention to the roof, basement, heating and cooling systems, structure, plumbing, and electrical. If the inspector finds any needed repairs, the buyer can negotiate for the costs of the repairs.

Next, you will enter escrow, which is a sort of limbo period between selling your home and receiving the money. You may remember this step from buying your home, though rather than putting money down, your role is now to hold up your end of the agreement. During this time, you and your agent will work with an escrow company to complete paperwork and ensure that all parts of the contract are complete.

On a predetermined closing date, you and your buyer will sit down with your agents to sign all the paperwork and pay all your fees. You will relinquish your keys and your property title, and you will receive a check for the remaining balance after the remainder of your mortgage is paid to your bank. Congrats - you have sold your home!

Once you and the buyer have agreed upon an offer, you will both sign a legal contract called a Purchase and Sale Agreement. This outlines the specific terms, conditions, and contingencies of the home sale.

Next, the buyer will hire an inspector to ensure that no major repairs will be needed after they buy the house. The inspector will go through every inch of the house, paying particular attention to the roof, basement, heating and cooling systems, structure, plumbing, and electrical. If the inspector finds any needed repairs, the buyer can negotiate for the costs of the repairs.
Next, you will enter escrow. During this time, you and your agent will work with an escrow company to complete paperwork and ensure that all parts of the contract are complete.

On a predetermined closing date, you and your buyer will sit down with your agents to sign all the paperwork and pay all your fees. You will relinquish your keys and your property title, and you will receive a check for the remaining balance after the remainder of your mortgage is paid to your bank. Congrats - you have sold your home!

Thinking of selling your home in Treasure Coast? It's important to understand that if you expect to make money on your home, you've got to give yourself plenty of time to prepare, and that can mean starting to plan months ahead of the date you'd actually like to move out of your home. Here's a timeline that covers what to expect before, during, and after you list your home in Treasure Coast.

Before Listing Your Home in Treasure Coast

To successfully sell a home, you can't just stick a For Sale sign in the front yard; you need to put in a little pre-work first! Here's what needs to happen before you even list your home for sale.

2+ Months Out:

Find an Experienced Treasure Coast Agent

This is a crucial first step! Enlisting the help of an experienced agent who understands your needs to guide you through the process will save you time and a lot of headache - and will of course get your home sold more quickly and for more money than trying to list your home on your own.

Find out more about our qualifications and experience!

6-8 Weeks Out:

Consider Repairs and Improvements

Your real estate agent will do a thorough walkthrough of your home and will likely make recommendations on both minor and major repairs or improvements you should consider. Additionally, you should be proactive about any known maintenance issues to your home, as these will surface during an inspection.

Value-boosting home improvements can include projects such as painting your home (inside or outside), refinishing hardwood floors, fixing or replacing your roof or siding, installing a new garage door or front door, doing some gardening or landscaping, updating or repairing your HVAC system, or even performing minor kitchen and bathroom repairs, such as updating flooring, resurfacing cabinets, installing new hardware and fixtures, and replacing or resurfacing countertops.

4-8 Weeks Out:

Set the Price Right

Another crucial step to ensuring the highest return when you sell your home is finding a competitive price. You will want to consider the price of nearby homes that have recently sold, the prices of nearby homes currently on the market, and the condition and location of your specific home. Request a neighborhood sold report and work with your real estate agent to find the right listing price.

1-4 Week(s) Out:

Prep Your Home

Hopefully, you have already started decluttering some of the bigger collections of unused furniture and other items stored in your attic, basement, or closets. Continue to work through your home, removing clutter, junk, and even personal decor. Start deep cleaning your home, really targeting the nooks and crannies.

Then, work with your agent to stage your home so that it is neat, welcoming, and depersonalized (allowing your buyers to picture their own personal touches in their potential new home).

Lastly, take professional photographs that will highlight your home's best features and give buyers a great impression of your home - right from their computer, tablet, or phone.

The Selling Process Of Your Treasure Coast Home

All right! You've done all the prep work, and now for the actual process of showing and selling your home. Here's what to expect once your home actually hits the market, and that For Sale sign appears in the front yard.

Market Your Home:

The key to selling a home is in finding the right buyers, and that requires a lot of marketing and advertising. This is where working with a skilled agent can really pay off. Skilled listing agents are skilled marketers. They know where to find the best buyers for your home, and they have access to a wealth of resources, including online listing services, print advertising distribution, large social media followings, and even local agent networks.

Show Your Home:

In addition to scheduled open houses, your home can be shown at any time, so be prepared. Keep it neat, clean, organized, and staged. Don't leave dirty dishes or laundry lying around, be sure to dust and vacuum regularly, and promptly address any potential clutter buildups. Additionally, you should be ready to clear out of the house during showings to avoid making buyers uncomfortable.

Negotiate and Accept:

If a buyer wants to buy your home, they will make you a written offer, which usually states how much they'll pay, their mortgage amount, closing and occupancy dates, and any contingencies. You can either accept the offer or negotiate for different terms.

Negotiations can include your own contingencies, such as a first right of refusal if your buyer's offer is contingent on selling their home, making the offer contingent on you buying another home, or adding contingencies for closing and occupancy dates or buyer financing.

The inspector will go through every inch of the house, paying particular attention to the roof, basement, heating and cooling systems, structure, plumbing, and electrical. Next, you will enter escrow. During this time, you and your agent will work with an escrow company to complete paperwork and ensure that all parts of the contract are complete.

Sign, Pay, and Finalize!

On a predetermined closing date, you and your buyer will sit down with your agents to sign all the paperwork and pay all your fees. blocks.text: Dubbed ‘The Jewel of the Isle’ when it opened its doors in 1988, the Empress still proudly reflects its nickname almost twenty five years later.An intimate community of 117 units, the Empress has a reputation for being a welcoming, safe and well run residence.

Upon entering the bright and open Lobby, you notice tropical yet sophisticated furniture accessorized with potted palms, bromeliads and other tropical plants. The newly refurbished elevators will bring you to the second floor, where unlike other condos, you will find the Social Room, Exercise Room and a large pool area. Looking out over the dune the newly renovated Social Room reflects the same tropical feel of the Lobby. A large bar and service areas are topped with granite and the walls filled with photos on stretched canvases that reflect the wildlife and landscapes of the Island. The unique second floor pool area provides an ocean view framed by palms and sea grapes. In addition to basking in the sun, ample shade is provided to read or enjoy table games.

In addition to its lovely surroundings, the Empress residents are the most important part of what makes the Empress “esteemed.” Many original owners and their families are either full-time residents or snowbirds. In season many renters have been returning for 15 years to participate and enjoy in the camaraderie, games, dinners and special events. New faces are always welcome and soon become a part of the Empress family.

blocks.text: Nettles Island, just north of the Martin/St. Lucie line on Hutchinson Island, is an interesting enclave of snowbirds, native Floridians, newbie Floridians, wannabe Floridians and vacationers who found this place by luck and could never give it up. What began as a campground in the late 1960s has evolved into more than 40 acres of custom homes, mobile homes, manufactured homes, Key West-style homes, built on stilts and RVs.
There are 1,578 properties on Nettles Island, which is connected to A1A by the main road, Nettles Boulevard.

Amenities are outrageous; there are two swimming pools (one on the ocean), tennis courts, clubhouse, bocce ball, shuffleboard. There are more than 40 clubs — everything from the kayak club to the yacht club to the men’s club and the women’s club. Line dancing is a big deal. Residents are super proud of their recycling efforts and socializing is an important part of everyday life, especially during the winter. Volunteer work is also important.
Nettles Island operates as a condo with a homeowners board. Nettles Island also has a marina, which can accommodate boats with a deep-water draw.

blocks.text: A planned community, Spring Valley in Altamonte Springs, Florida, is situated 10 miles north of the heart of downtown Orlando. This upscale community of 470 homes, has lovely tree-lined streets and the 84-acre Spring Lake at its center with restaurants and shopping nearby. It is an established community with strong neighborhood ties and estate style homes that vary in architectural styles with some homes facing Spring Lake or having in-ground pools. Homes range from 1,800 square feet to 5,400 square feet in living area, typically with 3-5 bedrooms and lot sizes of a quarter to a half-acre.

Community amenities in Spring Valley include a fishing pier for fishing and boating, dock with boat ramp access to the 84 acre skiable Spring Lake, Spring Valle Park, a private park with picnic pavilion and BBQ facility, playground, and basketball, volleyball and tennis courts.

Spring Valley is conveniently located near Uptown Altamonte, shopping, entertainment, and major highways, on the west side of I-4, just south of SR436 (Semoran Blvd). Maitland Blvd is nearby as is an entrance to I-4 which will take you North to Lake Mary, Sanford and eventually Daytona where it merges into I-95 or South to Orange County, Downtown Orlando, the attractions area and eventually Tampa where it merges into I-275. It is also easily accessible to SR- 429, SR-408 and SR-528 to Orlando International Airport.

Shopping, medical facilities and entertainment are nearby. Gateway Crossing shopping center, anchored by Publix, is within neighborhood boundaries. A couple of miles northeast is the much larger Altamonte Springs Mall, a two-story mall with a little over 1 million square feet of shopping plus an IMAX AMC theater and restaurants. For your health care needs, AdventHealth Altamonte Springs is less than 5 miles away and is part of a group of award-winning hospitals and medical centers in central Florida. New Smyrna Beach is the closest beach.

/neighborhood/mirabay.name: Mirabay
/neighborhood/mirabay.title: Mirabay
/neighborhood/mirabay.description: Search Homes For Sale in Mirabay in Apollo Beach.

blocks.text: Manns Harbor Drive Apollo Beach, FL 33572

Mirabay, Apollo Beach's premier luxurious waterfront gated community gives its residents access to an array of features like yacht-lined canals, private beaches, 18 holes of golfing at Copperhead Course, pristine swimming pools and waterfront parks.

Situated amidst the sparkling waters of Tampa Bay, Florida and among the scenery of the 1,300-acre Wolf Branch Creek Nature Preserve, MiraBay has 1,700 homes with residents of all ages. The unique combination of low-maintenance single family homes, desirable amenities and a socially active lifestyle make this community appealing to many homebuyers. Homes range in size from three to five bedrooms, two to four bathrooms, with two to three-car garages and feature floor plans from 1,924 to 5,863 square feet in living area. Of the five luxury home builders, three offer a variety of delightful and upscale floor plans, while David Weekley Homes and Sabal Homes offer buyers the opportunity to build fully custom homes. Many of the homesites in Mirabay offer water views or even private boat slips with ocean access.

Situated on 750 lushly landscaped acres, only 20 miles south of Tampa and near Old Tampa Bay, this community offers a high standard of living with resort-style amenities. With its proximity to the sea, Mirabay has boating access to the Gulf and residents can go fishing, sailing or swimming from their backyards. The resort-style Mirabay Club includes dedicated lap swimming lanes, a water slide, beach entry and a designated toddler pool. The Galley Cafe offers burgers, sandwiches and salads for poolside enjoyment as well as Happy Hour at sunset. The fully equipped fitness center with weight-training equipment and cardio equipment such as Vision treadmills, upright and recumbent bikes, stair climbers, and Matrix ellipticals. Personal training and group fitness classes are available to all residents. There are classes to include studio cycling, yoga and Pilates. In addition, the gym offers nutritional counseling for optimization of a healthy lifestyle. Outdoors residents have plenty of opportunities amongst the five lit tennis courts, sand volleyball and basketball courts. Nature lovers can take bike rides along the preserve, relax by the lagoon and fish from the pier. Water enthusiasts can cruise the Mangroves by grabbing a sunfish sailboat or kayak from The Outfitters Bait and Tackle Shop, which provides Mirabay residents with outstanding customer service.

Located in Apollo Beach along the Gulf Coast, Mirabay is in close proximity to Sarasota and Tampa Bay restaurants, theaters, museums, art venues and plenty of shops. Orlando's world-class attractions and the sandy beaches on the coastal islands of Sanibel, Anna Maria, Captiva and Longboat Key are popular day trip destinations in the vicinity. Apollo Beach, as a small resort town, lends itself to wildlife watching, especially at the Manatee Viewing Center and the Apollo Beach Nature Park.

Royal Palm Yacht & Country Club is an exclusive golf and waterfront community in eastern Boca Raton, located along the west side of the intracoastal waterway, south of Camino Real Blvd. and south to the Boca Raton / Deerfield Beach city lines.

Royal Palm's estate homes feature waterfront, golf course, or garden views, private dockage, outdoor kitchens overlooking resort-style private swimming pools, 3+ car garages, and a multitude of additional high-end features custom to each estate. Royal Palm Yacht Club is an exclusive club founded in 1959 that has long been an integral part of the East Boca Raton landscape. It's members enjoy the convenience of a premium location minutes from the Boca Inlet and across from the world-renowned Boca Raton Resort and Club. The exclusive community offers waterfront, golf course, and interior properties with over 450 acres of land and 700 estate homes. Royal Palm's estate homes feature waterfront, golf course, or garden views, private dockage, outdoor kitchens overlooking resort-style private swimming pools, 3+ car garages, and a multitude of additional high-end features custom to each estate.

An epicenter for the affluent, Royal Palm Yacht and Country Club, members have an array of amenities including a full yacht club and marina with dock master that can accommodate yachts up to 120 feet,18-hole well maintained golf course, 6 Har-Tru tennis courts, croquet courts, a well-equipped modern fitness facility, pool and spa and a variety of dining options including 5-star restaurants.

Membership in Royal Palm Yacht Club is not limited to residents of the community and is a private invitation only Club. New members must be invited by 2 current members of the club. There are 2 levels of membership: Full Golf and Social, and each level of membership offers a Junior and Legacy membership for those between 24 and 39 years old.

blocks.text: The Inlets is a planned gated and highly desirable waterfront coastal community in Bradenton, Florida. With access to the Gulf of Mexico and deep-water docks, residents enjoy an exclusive lifestyle where they can keep a boat in their own backyard. The Inlets are located just north of Sarasota, off I-75 in Bradenton, set a new standard for waterfront living. Developed with boating in mind, most of the luxurious homes are set along the Manatee River or freshwater canals with deep water dockage. Hundred year old oaks and pines add to the area's natural splendor, making this a special neighborhood. There are three neighborhoods within The Inlets: Bella Sole, Harbour Walk and The Reserve. Home designs are inspired by Caribbean, Mediterranean, Nantucket, and Sarasota styles. For those looking for worry-free living, the Bella Sole Courtyard offers maintenance-free living with reasonable quarterly fees. Buyers looking for something more palatial can choose residences at The Reserve or the luxurious Harbour Walk. These two neighborhoods offer far grander waterfront amenities, such as private docks and boat launches that can take sailors out to the sparkling waters of the Gulf of Mexico.

Many of the amenities at The Inlets are centered on nature and aquatic activities. Amenities within the community include kayak and canoe launches, fishing pier, tennis courts, nature-filled trails, observation spots, a picnic area with tables and benches a children's playground and hiking and jogging trails. Its diverse downtown area offers an array of attractions and a charming historic district and main street, with entertainment at the museum and performing arts center. The neighborhood is surrounded by tennis clubs and golf courses.

The area also spotlights a variety of restaurants and one-of-a-kind boutiques. There are stunning scenes on the famous Riverwalk, which offers views of the Manatee River or the Robinson Preserve featuring lovely trails, a boat ramp and observation platforms. A colorful locale within Bradenton, the Village of the Arts is lined with vibrant cottages that include bakeries and shops as well as galleries and studios that display the work of many talented artists. Locals and tourists will love the choice of breathtaking beaches and nearby Anna Maria Island offers postcard-like panoramas.

blocks.text: On Top of the World Clearwater

On Top of the World is a unique and lovely 55 plus retirement community located just off Belcher Road in Clearwater, Florida. This location is convenient to shopping, dining and entertainment, and has easy access to public transportation. It is a pet friendly community. This age-restricted community consists of 96 condo buildings with a low-maintenance lifestyle. On Top of the World Clearwater has 96 condo buildings with a total of 4,959 units. Condo units consisting of 1-2 bedrooms range from about 850 square feet to 1,750 square feet.

On Top of the World features a community bus that has scheduled trips to local shopping as well all around Clearwater. The community amenities include their own golf course, which residents enjoy for free, tennis courts, swimming pools, fitness center and hobby shops. Many indoor activities including ceramics, tai chi, wood shop and bridge are also offered.

The main clubhouse is the East Recreation Center that houses the majority of the amenities for residents to use. The East Recreation Center has a fitness center, aerobics studio, billiards, library, computer room, card room, poker room, and catering kitchen, a heated outdoor pool, four tennis courts, eight horseshoe pits, twelve shuffleboard courts, and lawn bowling. Residents enjoy two golf courses, an 18-hole golf course and a 9-hole course. There are plenty of craft rooms like a woodworking shop, ceramics, lapidary, and arts and crafts studio. Homeowners can grab a quick bite to eat at the Good Karma Cafe.

The West Recreation Center features a fitness center, indoor spa, billiards room, multi-purpose room, and card room, outdoor pool and spa, lounge on the patio, or take their pet for a stroll at the dog park. A fishing pier and lake provide an area for residents to kayak, fish, or canoe.

Situated in Clearwater, Florida, On Top of the World Clearwater offers active adult homeowners a convenient location near everyday conveniences. The community is close to Highway 19, with many shopping options. There is access to parks for recreation like Moccasin Lake Nature Park, Northeast Coachman Park, and Cliff Stephens Park. Great medical facilities can be found at Morton Plant Hospital that's only seven miles away. The St. Petersburg International Airport is less than ten miles away.

blocks.text: Set amid the many lakes for which it was named, Ridgewood Lakes Village in Davenport, Florida offers a tight-knit suburban lifestyle for its residents. Ridgewood lakes has a main entrance on Highway 27. Palm trees are scattered between homes along residential streets, offering shade to well-manicured lawns and driveways with attached garages. They also feature a pool, spa 6 shuffleboard courts, 2 tennis courts, and walking trails. Davenport is defined by its lakeside activities, boating and fishing, and golfing.

Nearby theme parks include Universal Studios and Disney World as well as the more populous cities of Orlando and Tampa. Davenport is a commuter city; Interstate 4 and U.S. Highway 27 provide convenient access to Orlando and Tampa, 33 and 60 miles away, respectively.

The community consists of 450 single-family homes and golf villas of Oyster Creek Golf and Country Club built on and around a challenging 18 hole executive golf course. blocks.text: Located on the barrier islands close to Englewood and Venice, Manasota Key is a pristine 11 mile island. Access to the island is across two bridges over the Intracoastal Waterway, one at the north end in Sarasota County, and one to the south in Charlotte County. Quite a few of the properties enjoy water views with the most sought-after homes being located right on the Gulf, while others offer views of Lemon Bay and the small isles of Stump Pass Beach State Park and the Lemon Bay Aquatic Preserve. This island offers breathtaking waterfront views that embody the pinnacle of Florida coast living with homes that boast vast sizes and stunning architectural designs making the area a beacon for those seeking an affluent community.

Between condos and single-family residences, there are only about 1,000 homes on the island, some are million-dollar New England mansions that sit right in front of the beach. Some homes have private docking space along the many canals around the island. Manasota Key features four beaches with a variety of facilities offering beach goers and boaters a tropical setting. A canopy of trees covers the two lane road as it winds along the island. Private residences are tucked away behind lush tropical foliage, some extending from Gulf to Bay.

In general, pricing in Manasota Key is very affordable when compared to other beach communities in Southwest Florida. The area still has many quaint beach bungalows and cottages tucked away behind the dense vegetation. These charming homes swap cavernous interiors for raise deck areas, longer drives, and affordability and are less than 1,000 square feet. Manasota Key still has its fair share of low-rise condos and gated villa communities that is not as heavily developed as other areas around Venice and Sarasota. In these developments you will be able to enjoy high-quality amenities, including pools, tennis courts, beach access, private docks, and facility rentals.

Residential zoning dominates this part of town, although there are a few seafood restaurants and pubs along North Beach Road. Driving to South Englewood for groceries does not take long at all; the Merchants Crossing shopping center, which is anchored by a remodeled Publix supermarket, is less than 10 minutes away.

Between condos and single-family residences, there are only about 1,000 homes on the island, some are million-dollar New England mansions that sit right in front of the beach. Some homes have private docking space along the many canals around the island. Manasota Key features four beaches with a variety of facilities offering beach goers and boaters a tropical setting. A canopy of trees covers the two lane road as it winds along the island. Private residences are tucked away behind lush tropical foliage, some extending from Gulf to Bay.

In general, pricing in Manasota Key is very affordable when compared to other beach communities in Southwest Florida. The area still has many quaint beach bungalows and cottages tucked away behind the dense vegetation. These charming homes swap cavernous interiors for raise deck areas, longer drives, and affordability and are less than 1,000 square feet. Manasota Key still has its fair share of low-rise condos and gated villa communities that is not as heavily developed as other areas around Venice and Sarasota. In these developments you will be able to enjoy high-quality amenities, including pools, tennis courts, beach access, private docks, and facility rentals.

Residential zoning dominates this part of town, although there are a few seafood restaurants and pubs along North Beach Road. Driving to South Englewood for groceries does not take long at all; the Merchants Crossing shopping center, which is anchored by a remodeled Publix supermarket, is less than 10 minutes away.

blocks.text: Englewood Isles is a deed restricted boating neighborhood with waterfront opportunities for fishing and boating right at your doorstep. It is a vibrant tropical community with private Marina and access to expansive Lemon Bay. Englewood Isles provides direct boating admittance through the Windsor and Waterford Canals.

A very quiet part of town surrounded by lush and mature greenery, Englewood Isles is located about two miles south of the section of Tamiami Trail that turns east towards the Florida Everglades. There are six sections containing more than 500 homes, including condos, villas and single-family residences with Florida ranch-style homes with lots of interior space, some homes featuring 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms with more than 1,900 square feet of living space. Homes vary from 2-5 bedrooms and range from 1,015 square feet to 6,546 square feet in living area. Each home is unique offering something for everyone. Englewood Isles offers its residents access to a private marina where docks are available for lease or to purchase. You can navigate your boat to the Gulf in no time as there are no bridges.

With five bodies of water around Englewood Isles, there are many waterfront properties, some are built alongside canals that connect to the Intracoastal Waterway. Many of these homes have private docking space and boat lifts and ramps for easy canal access while others have nice wooden piers for fishing and there is Forked Creek Marina, located right at the entrance of the community.

Englewood Isles has a secluded tropical feel but with very convenient location. The Lemon Bay shopping center is right across Englewood Road, and it features large stores such as Big Lots and Dollar Tree along with bakeries, pizzerias and healthcare clinics. Additional shopping can be found in the Venice Village Shoppes about five minutes away, next to the Venice East Golf Course. Manasota Beach and Englewood Beach are only a short 3-mile drive and the more pristine Blind Pass Beach and Duisberg Trail park are just a couple of miles south. Englewood Isles is close to restaurants, shopping and world-class golf courses. The Charlotte County Airport and Sarasota Airport are close by.
